title: Records, enums, match — the Vyrn guide

chapter.title: Records, enums, match
chapter.lede: A record is a shape. An enum is a choice. `match` covers every case, and the compiler counts them.

sections.heading: Records
prose: A record type lists fields. Compatibility is by shape: a value with more fields fits where fewer are wanted, with no cast and no base class. This is width subtyping, and it is the whole inheritance story.
Fields of a mut binding are assigned in place. A record that owns heap data — a String field, for example — is moved by an assignment, so copy() is how both sides keep a value.

sections.heading: Enums
prose: An enum value is exactly one variant, and a variant can carry a payload. There is no tag field to keep in step with a union, because the tag is the type.
match must cover every variant. Leave one out and the file does not compile. That is what makes an enum safe to extend: add a variant, and the compiler lists every place that has to answer for it.

sections.heading: match expressions
prose: match answers with a value, so a binding takes it directly and there is no mutable slot to fill in each arm.
if let reads one variant when the others need no arm. while let does the same in a loop, and stops when the pattern stops matching.
